I am always happy to stir up hornets nests, so here is a new point for the
endless CL vs NL debate. Now with the inclusion of the Sabbat set, what
is the point of continuing to use a 4CL, as now there are so many subtle
variation cards that there is effectively no limit in the 4CL. Sabbat has
substantially increased the redundancy in the card set, such that almost
all disciplines have the same redundancy as Obfuscate and Dominate did
originally. For instance, under CL, it has been historically difficult to
build an effective Rush Combat deck (i.e. one that can compete with the
Malk S+B deck). With the addition of the Sabbat set, it is almost easy to
make, for instance, a Pot Rush Combat deck:

4 Haven Uncovered
4 Bum Rush
4 Ambush

4 Torn Signpost
4 Fists of Death
4 Fire in the Blood

4 Undead Strength
4 Mighty Grapple
4 Pushing the Limit
4 Growing Fury
4 Pulled Fangs
4 Disarm
ect...

There is no imagintation needed to build this deck (as is often used as a
strong point of 4CL). You just put in 4 of every similar card and
shuffle. It is very similar to many NL combat decks, but perhaps you
would use 8 Undead Strength as opposed to 4 US and 4 PtL. The net result
is pretty much the same. If you wanted to use Celerity for additional
strikes, there are, like, 6 or 7 Cel cards that give additional strikes.
What is the difference, really, between using 4 of each or 24 of one?

The only difference between this 4CL deck and a non CL similar combat deck
is the lack of enough Immortal Grapples to combat the now 8 or 12
Strike:Combat Ends cards that Presence has.

My point is basicaly that with all the extra Sabbat cards that are very
similar to the regular cards (two types of Deflection. Two types of Skin
of Steel. Two Elder Interventions. Two WWEF. Multiple damaging
votes...), 4CL becomes something of a pointless design limit. You can now
make a "Degenerate" Gangrel Rush deck with 12 easy get into combat cards
(I am yet to see an effective NL rush deck that uses more than 15% get
into combat cards, and 12 is 15% of 80...) and 12 "Wolf Claws"; or any
sort of "Degenerate NL deck" you want. You can almost even make an
effective Brujah Pitch deck (almost...). The only cards that do not have
redundancy at this point are some of the obscure but useful cards like
Immortal Grapple and Vote modifiers, which are needed to combat other
types of decks that are unhindered by 4CL.

What do you all think?

The inclusion of the Sabbat cards seems to change 4CL to run like 6CL/10%
used to. All the basic deck types are there (especially rush combat, the
great lacuna of 4CL), just less variety (e.g., there are bleed bounce
decks, but only with both AUS and DOM - AUS- or DOM-only bounce doesn't
work reliably).

>My point is basicaly that with all the extra Sabbat cards that are very
>similar to the regular cards (two types of Deflection. Two types of Skin
>of Steel. Two Elder Interventions. Two WWEF. Multiple damaging
>votes...), 4CL becomes something of a pointless design limit.

4CL has always been an arbitrary, and not very effective, way to control
deck types. Obviously 4CL on Assault Rifle is much less of a limit than
4CL on Fake Out. And, as you point out, the presence of duplicates and
near substitutes has a big effect on the relevance of CLs too. The best
way to channel Jyhad decks would probably be minimum %'s of card types -
e.g. at least x% combat, y% actions, z% Masters etc. Because of
instant-redraw, minimum percentages are much more meaningful than
maximums. Limits on card purposes (no more than x% stealth) would be a
bear to define - too many grey-area and specialized cards.

This is not to say that such limitations are desirable, merely that they
would be more effective and less arbitrary.

Some anonymous person wrote:

"As for the "So many subtle variation cards"; I would like to refute this

As for "Subtle Variations", I mean cards that are just like another card,
just a little different. They have nothing to do with "Broken" cards.
The bulk of the new cards in Sabbat are "Subtle Variation" cards. I like
the "Subtle Variation" cards, and think they are the best cards in the
set, but that is what they are, "Subtle Variations". For instance,
"Pushing the Limit" vs. "Undead Strength", "Redirection" vs "Deflection",
and "Superior Mettle" vs "Skin of Steel", "Pursuit" vs "Nimble Feet".
These cards are very similar, but have enough difference to make you want
to use one over the other for a subtle reason. Under 4CL, having a choice
between PtL and US means "Oh good! Now I can have 8 first round POT
strikes." Undr NL, having a choice between PtL and US means "Ok, now
which do I want to use? US does less damage but costs no blood. PtL
Costs blood. Maybe I'll use 8 of one or 6 and 2..." The "Subtle
Variation" cards under NL allow for slight deck modifications but have no
overwhelming effect on the play environment. Under 4CL, the "Subtle
Variation" cards greatly affect the play environment ("Hey! Now I can
have EIGHT deflections!"), and the subtle differences have little meaning.
For instance, where in NL it may be significant to have 8 "Superior
Mettle" rather than 8 "Skin of Steel" (because you like to Press, for
instance...), in 4CL, you just are happy cause you now can have 4 of each,
effectively just having 8 "Skin of Steel".

He then wrote:
"1: certain cards are no longer broken (with a 4CL, 1 CL Uniques - as we
play). Examples - ToR, Blood to Water, Art Meseum etc."

Regardless of the debatability of the brokenness of the above mantioned

effect on the game slightly, but when they come up, they are still just as
busted.

And then he wrote:
"Well you seem to have found the second argument in favour of 4CL for me.
The challenge and skill required in deck building and in game play is
greater in CL."

Now mind you, my group played 4CL for a year or so, so I fully understand
what is involved in making 4CL decks, and all of the arguments in favor,
as I made them all (before I decided that I was wrong...:-). The main
skill and challange in building 4CL decks is figuring out how to get
around the card limit. Once you have exausted 4 of every useful card you
need, you spend the rest of the time trying to figure out how to make
other cards do what you want circumvent the limit. For instance,
everybody who has tried to build a Rush Combat deck under 4CL put in 4 Bum
Rush, 4 Haven Uncovered, and then when faced with "How do I get in combat
more often when I can only use 4 of each of these cards?" put in 4
Rampages, reasoning "Well, they'll have to block me if I go to Rampage on
their Art Museum..." (Cumon. Admit it . You all have :-). Show me a

just plug in the seasoning cards (CEL or OBF or DOM or whatever)

Anonymous wrote:
>
> >But now you can have 8 of those,
>

> strategies, such as Stealth and Bleed (S&B) are now ineffectual unless
> a deck can be made to the same high quality as the rest of our decks
> have been.

How is S&B ineffective? It is not so under NL. There was never any
attempt to restrict S&B. S&B is not a problem in NL. If, as you say,
S&B is ineffective under 4CL, there's another point against it.

> >while (for example) you can still only have 4 Immortal Grapples.
>
> So? Why is Immortal grapple so damned amazing? Yes its good against
> tremere.

Immortal Grapple stops Dodge and S:CE, and does it more effectively than
any of the cards you mention below.

> So does potence bung combat.

Who cares about beating up the Tremere? In general, IG is effective
against a large number of strategies.

> Yes it cuts down on combat ends. So do three
> other cards - Psyche, Fast reaction (for anintercept deck) and hidden
> lurker (for a rush deck).

But no deck will be able to play with more than one of these, and there

[4CL env. constantly changing]

> which makes the game much more exciting as it is always changing and
> adding depth and variety to the game, rather than sticking with a
> simple stagnant deck design for eternity, because it wins.

There is no NL deck which always wins.

Having 4CL when there are so many duplicates is pointless. It doesn't
fix anything, and puts a stranglehold on creativity.

> >"Oh, now I can have 8 Bum's Rush type cards, where before I
> >could only have 4." What's the point?

[answer: rush decks easier to make]

I understand that. My point is that why bother having this arbitrary
4CL when, in the case of "get into combat actions", it's really an 8CL.

> >It's like having selective 4/8/12/etc.-CL based on what has been
> >printed.
>
> Yes. And its the selective part that makes it so much better.

It's _better_ to have a random 4/8/12 CL depending on what's been
_printed_?

> WotC seem to
> have realised what the problems were with CL and have accounted for
> that with bringing out altered duplicates for all the areas where CL
> was left lacking.

WotC puts out a NL game. The "duplicates" of which you are so fond are
actually well-designed cards, unlike a lot of that set.

> Now there is no longer any problem with playing CL and the bonuses
> for playing it are still there.

Bonuses? What bonuses?

[ToR]

> If you use it to its most efficient then
> it will be an advantage to have more than one in, because you can

it, it will never be contested, and the person who happened to shuffle

> This is the reason why it is broken under NL

It's not any less broken under CL. In fact, as I argued above, it might
be more broken.

> under CL
> you are limited to having only one in the deck and may find that it
> will get unnatural disastered (as CL makes these cards worth having, 2
> pool to stop someone having a limitless continual blood supply is not

You think it's advantageous to know for sure how many card someone has
left in their deck? "Oh, you've used all 4 Majesties? I Bum's Rush
you..." Yeah, that's great fun.

> NL players saying that Blood to water is broken, under card limits it
> was not; not even when it could be played at long range!)

Blood to Water is not broken.

> Again I was only commenting on people saying that it was "annoying"
> which I took to been that it was slightly broken (Perhaps overpowered
> would be a better description?)

Annoying != Broken. Madness of the Bard is not broken, but boy, is it
annoying. Art Museum is not broken, but it is powerful. Why restrict
it?

> >Please defend this statement. I do not see how 4CL _increases_
> >necessary skill.
>
> Deck building:
> Under an NL environment you only need to think about what cards you
> want to put in your deck to make it work

Under a CL environment you only need to think about what cards you

> Under a CL

> areas, meaning that you will have to be a lot more careful,
> intelligent, skillful (or what ever you want to call it) at planning
> your deck so that you can rely on it working to
> close to its maximum efficiency all the time.

that you have more freedom. How does lack of freedom to decide increase
creativity?

other cards to put in your deck that circumvent the limit. So if all of
the effort is spent trying to get around the limit, why have it?

> Game Playing:
> Under CL, because your deck is so much more "highly strung" (as one NL
> player put it) than a comparative NL deck, you will have to makesure
> that all your cards are used to their best value

So you sit around doing nothing until you get exactly the right
combination of cards in your hand (i.e., "gin")? Woo hoo. Sounds like
fun to me.

> - a combat is only
> successful if you can manage to torporise or burn an opponent (or
> escape unharmed if that is your aim), etc.

This is true in NL too. If you didn't escape unharmed, then you were
probably sent to torpor or burned.

> If you waste too many cards
> on frivolous failiures then you will be destined to loose.

So what happens when a combat deck gets in a fight with a deck which
wants to "escape unharmed"? According to you, one of them is "destined
to lose". So table position determines victory? This is true to some
extent in NL, but not to this degree.

> Under CL
> you need to utilise what you have to the best of its capability,
> rather than under NL where the majority
> the tactics are in deck construction.

^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
Thank you. That's because deck construction in 4CL is mindless and
pointless.

> A CL deck that has to discard is probably
> a bad CL deck.

So the mighty, creative, wonderful 4CL deck _never_ hand jams? Yeah,
right.

> >I am making a Brujah rush combat deck. How many Torn Signpost? 4.
> >How many Undead Strength? 4. Etc. With NL, you have to decide how
> >many you need.
>
> Yes, so you will have more than four in an NL deck. There is very
> little difference; the advantage you gain from adding more cards I can
> gain from reducing the size of my deck (which is a much harder task,
> IMO).

No, you _might_ have more in a NL deck. At least you get to choose.
I'm not saying that every 4CL deck has 4 of everything, but you
certainly are not going to have any _less_ than 4 Bum's Rushes in a 4CL
rush deck.

> Well, now you could add pushing the limit which would give you 8,
> reduce your deck size down from what it would be, and make sure that
> when you are playing the game that each and evry card counts for
> something.

The deck is 80 cards. [But then, maybe you brought the 60-card deck
limit over from Magic, too.]

What if I don't _want_ to play with Pushing the Limit? 4CL forces me to
play with it if I want to be competitive. With 4CL, you _have_ to buy
significant amounts of every expansion, just to stay competitive.

> >Not really. With Rush combat reasonably effective, the Setites
> >become the worse problem. My Pre/Obf deck doesn't have more than 6
> >of anything, and even under 4CL would be quite effective, since I
> >don't use many of the new Sabbat Pre bleed cards. With only 4 IG or
> >4 Psyche, S:CE will win most of the time.
>
> Okay... S:CE, yes it is a problem.

...which it is not under NL.

> No its not deadly. you can have 4
> different cards that will counter S:CE (Psyche, Hidden Lurker, Fast
> reaction and Immortal Grapple)

...which no deck will be able to use all of.

> Presence has, to my knowledge, 2
> different S:CE cards,

Three, with Staredown.

> and any rush deck that can use up these cards is actually doing well.

But didn't you say that if a deck that wants to beat people up in combat
fails to do so, they are "destined to lose"? It sounds like Majesty is

> How does it work with these vampires? you have 4 different vampires

[snip: smack talking]

You claim that all of my vampires would be in torpor constantly. Quite

>

Well, no.

> addition to everything above you also have to remember that you are

>
> In that case it would probably end up being far to large and wouldn't
> get anything it needed through quickly enough,

OK, when I say "4 of everything", I don't literally mean 4 of every
single card in the game.

My point is (which I made earlier and you chose to ignore) that in a 4CL
Brujah rush deck, you would be a fool not to put in 4 of the following:

Bum's Rush
Ambush
Haven Uncovered
Undead Strength
Torn Signpost
Immortal Grapple
Flash
Blur

There's 32 cards that _must_ go in. No thought involved. The rest of

environment (i.e., I don't have any of card X in my hand, since I only
have 4, so I'm useless).

> it would have to refuse
> to block something

Does this indicate that a combat must rely on blocking actions to get
into combat? Gosh, sounds like stealth still is the most effective
strategy.

> Deck creation in CL is as

> much about balance as it is under NL, the only difference is that you
> have to obtain that in ways that, IMO, are more challenging to
> obtain.

"Challenging" and "difficult" are two different things.

> So, your saying that its just down to a point of principle? Who am I
> to tell you what to do, sort of thing? Well, that swings both ways:
> why can't I restrict myself if I like that better.

As long as you see that it's an arbitrary restriction with no overall
redeeming value.

> All the people I
> play with feel the same so its not a huge problem for us. I'm not
> trying to get you to play CL, okay, so might I think that your life
> might be slightly better if you did, but its not my place to tell you
> that, so I won't.

But you just did. I could go up to you and say "I could tell you that
you're an idiot, but I won't". [Just kidding]

I still don't see what 4CL fixes. You claim that it obviates the need
for the GT, but I don't see that either. Vote pushing is still very,
very effective.

> The point that I would debate with here is that
> placing a CL on a game makes it less creative, perhaps it does to a
> certain extent, but I think that really this is not true, when you get
> down to the bare bones of it: I doubt that there is any
> deck that would be uncreatable under CL that is creatable under NL
> (barring One-Trick-Ponies), I think that its all a matter of how you
> look at it.

You cannot make any NL deck under 4CL because NL decks will have more
than 4 of something.

> Rather than saying "I've not got enough of this card so I can't make
> that deck work", think instead "How can I make this deck work? What
> other cards can I use to emulate this effect?" That is where the
> creativity and the
> challenge comes in to deck building under CL.

That is where the craftiness and difficulty come.

I don't see having to try really hard to get around a self-imposed limit
as being creative at all.

> >You wouldn't want to play against them? Why? OTP's are notoriously
> >vulnerable to their anti-pony (i.e. WVP/WPV vulnerable to Atonement).
>
> What is WVP/WPV?

Weenie Vote Push / Weenie Presence Vote.

> do you mean that I have to make a deck that counters another deck
> deliberately? Or have to use a sideboard to counter any OTPs that
> might crop up? Either of these ideas I find distasteful! (infact it
> was one of your NL lot - Curt Adams, I think - who has written an
> article that can be found on Judith and Marks web page about why side
> boards are inappropriate)

My point was not that sideboards are a good idea (I think that they are
_not_), but that any OTP is easily defeatable by a well-designed deck,
i.e., one that is built with many strategies in mind.

> This is my point about the Sabbat expansion. Now the things that 4CL
> breaks are gone! All its problems have been completely obliterated by
> this expansion and we can now go on and play 4CL with out you lot
> saying "S&B! S&B! S&B! S&B!!!" at us all the time - there is no longer
> any problem with 4CL apart from principle, and GT also has breaks a
> principle aswell, so now we truely are even!

The problems with 4CL, as I have outlined them above:

* S&B still a major swing strategy. [Especially with Setites.]
* Stifles creativity and freedom of deck construction.
* S:CE [anti-combat in general]
* Required to buy every expansion to stay competitive
* Counting cards in ash heap becomes valuable
* CL varies based on cards in print

> >What you describe is a One Trick Pony.
>
> No. What I describe is an effective OTP (as S&B used to be under the
> old 4CL before Sabbat).

That's what I said.

> But if a deck is to deal with a truely degenerate OTP (ie. one that
> can destroy you very quickly), then you will need a sideboard, which
> will reduce the challenge and creativity of deck building

You would _not_ need a sideboard. When a deck is made, you should make
considerations for what other decks might be your predator/prey. Any
deck should be able to deal with Bleed, Vote and Combat. If not, then
that deck is not well-designed.

> I can't see any OTP's that would work effectively under
> 4CL therefore its not a problem for me.

I still claim that the Obf/Pre deck would be very effective.

> >Unfortunately, one thing 4CL decks are not is well-designed.
>
> This is an insulting statement that is both unfounded and untrue.
> I expect this statement to be withdrawn.

No. I was not insulting you. I truly believe that it is impossible to
make a well-designed deck in 4CL. The card limit itself limits design
possibilities.

James

to me. Problem cards don't get duplicated...non-problem cards (like cards

thing I wanted to interject was this: I'm not trying to say that CL is a
better way to play than NL. Which style you prefer is subjective...neither
one is "better" than the other. Many people like playing CL. For some

trying to see the other side. I have played under both CL and NL, and I

Any action type described in the rulebook is a "type" of action.
These are:
* Bleed
* Hunt
* Equip
* Transfer Equipment (this may be the same as equip, but I don't think so)
* Employ (Retainer)
* Recruit (Ally)
* Call a vote (PA)
* Rescue from Torpor
* Diablerize (in Torpor)
* Leave Torpor

Every other action is a "type" by card name. Rush and Ambush are
different types, therefore.

Also, every action permitted by a card in play is its own type,
distinct from every other card-in-play action (even of the same
name). So, entering combat with Rake via a Haven Uncovered on
Rake is a different type than Haven Uncovered on Anvil (or even
a second Haven Uncovered on Rake). This paragraph is subject
to change (hopefully), but is currently official.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson

CLA...@leeds.ac.uk (DPH) writes:
>>CL does for Jyhad what a strict rhyme/meter does for writing: it
>>requires a certain kind of creativity that some people enjoy, but
>>it severely restricts what you can do. Some people like poetry,
>>some don't. However, if you're in competition (arguing a legal
>>case, say), speaking in verse will put you at a disadvantage. And
>>there's plenty of room for creativity without adopting an
>>arbitrary restriction. (My opinion, CL proponents disagree, of course.)

>A very eloquent analogy!

Quite an insiteful one, at that.

However, rhyme/meter restrictions typically force a writer into
using more obscure words (via a thesaurus, or by grace of an
over-developed vocabulary). This increases variety, both within
a poem and between poems.

CL restrictions typically force a deck-builder into certain patterns
of card usages: 4 each of the "good" cards even marginally related to
the desired deck, and then a handful of flavor cards. Limiting
to four increases the variety within a deck, but decreases the
variations betweem decks.

Poetry extends the vocabulary into new areas, CL restricts the
card usage to predicable sets.

All cardless actions represent a "type" of action. All actions (even
carded ones) of that type are the same type.

Any action card action of a type not represented by a cardless action

is a "type" by card name.

Any action granted by a card in play is a type distinct to that instance
of the card.

The rule is "A minion cannot attempt an action of a type that he has
already attempted this turn."

Nathan Harada <i...@hula.net> writes:

> This is interesting. Could you explain to me why Majesty and
>Obedience are examples of semi-broken cards? Thanks.

Simply put, the cards are better than the alternatives (Dodge), almost
completely hose combat decks in large enough quantities, and can generally
be disposed of without much trouble, so no hand jam. Disposing of
Obedience does require an intercept deck.

Obedience decks are rare enough that people can ignore them, but Majesty
decks force combat decks to carry large quantities of anti-S:CE cards.
They are semi-broken in that they do not break the game, but do warp many
decks to cope with their existance.

You'll note that almost all serious objections to NL today revolve around
decks heavily reliant on cards that provide S:CE and untap, or have a
similar effect (Obedience and Deflection).

<<<<<<<<SNIP!>>>>>>

Uhmmmm.... last time I checked there *are* statistics in chess. Ever had
to calculate the probabilty of a move in your head? That is using
statistics....

>
> > In chess you have a limit to the # of pieces of certain
> > types that you are allowed to use, each with there own capabilities and
> > some are better than others, ie- a queen is better than a pawn, is a
> > statement I think most people will agree with. So, in NL you can, by
> > inductive reasoning, say that you may have 20 "queens" in your deck,
> > whereas in CL you may only be allowed 4 or 5 such "queens". Just got
> > more tricky didn't it? You suddenly have a finite amount of "queen"
> > resources and have to watch how you play them, making a CL game more like
> > a game of chess. This is not to say that CL games are anything like a
> > fine game of chess, just more analagous to it than NL games are. How we
> Hmm, I'm confused. If CL games aren't like a game of chess, then
> why that example? Actually, NL games are far more like chess than CL
> games, because luck plays a much smaller role in NL games than CL games.

Couldn't disagree more. Since you missed the boat entirely, I'll restate
it again:

In chess you have a finite number of pieces, ie- one queen, one king,
etc. We can all agree that a queen is better than a pawn. Using
inductive reasoning we can say that a NL deck can have 20 "queens" in
it. In a CL deck you can have only 4 or 5 such "queens" in it, thereby
approaching a game more like chess than NL since you have finite number
of pieces of any given type to choose from.

Where we seemed to have diverged was saying that CL are not exactly like
chess. You seemed to have taken my statement previously too literally,
thereby dismissing an entire analogy. My point in the end is that CL
games are more like chess than NL, given the premise of a finite # of
pieces of any given type.

You raise an interesting counterpoint however. You seem to be saying
that NL is more like chess in that when you stack your deck with 20 WweF
you *know* that you will get this card, in the same way that in chess you
know that you will get one queen. Let's carry this further.

Let's suppose that WweF is the best card in the game (some would say it
is, but that is another argument). Once again using inductive reasoning,
we can say that a WweF card would be analagous to a "queen", arguably the
best piece in chess. Using the argument presented by you, NL decks would
be more like chess since you know you will get WweF in your hand at any
given time, or in this case, the "queen" will always be at your disposal
for use. How is this like chess? You don't always get to use the queen,
some games if you are *really* unfortunate you won't get to use her at all!

In the end I see your point that NL is like chess in that with it you
will know that you will get a certain card in your hand, much the same
way you know you will play with one queen in chess, and I agree with you
on that point. However, I disagree with you in saying that having 20
"queens" in a jyhad deck is anything like chess at all since since there
is no finite limit to your resources like there is in chess.

Why all the comparison to chess? Well, I had hoped to avoid a direct
comparison, and that is not what I want to cast about as my premise. I
am only using chess as analogy to the finite # of resources you have when
you play Jyhad with CL. We can all agree that chess is nothing at all
like Jyhad, whether or not we play NL or CL. However, it is still a
useful analogy to look at to see why some people would want to play with
CL rules.

I personally still prefer NL games due to time issues and the fact that
if I really wanted to play a game like chess, I'd just go play chess....
Also, there is one final reason I prefer NL games over CL games; the
omnipresent "Wheeeeee!!!!..." fun factor that CL seem to lack. ;>

Okay. J. Hamlin (JH) wrote a hell of a lot of stuff, and I don't want to do
another 850 post length, so I'll just summerise and counter at the end. I
hope this will make this shorter and easy to follow. However I realise that
I may miss interperate some points, so please feel free to correct me if I
have botched.

1. I pointed out that If someone has a far superior deck then that deck
would win (Ths was after a long thread about how expansions changing the
environment under CL is good in my opinion and bad in JH's). JH said that
there was no such deck.

This presumably means that JH's group is evenly matched - if it was not
there could well be one player who could make a vastly superior deck and
beat them all all the time. Unless JH is refering to the fact that all NL
decks are by definition balanced and that there is no advantage to being a
more skillful player (in this unlikely scenario there is nio point competing
as it would just be down to luck who won)

1a. JH said, with reference to point (1) above, that why continue to play CL
when the expansions make the game tend towards a NL environment.

Because they add variety and flavour, and bring in more of the World of
Darkness (from the roleplaying games - which we all play) with every
expansion.

1b. JH asked if no one plays S&B in our group.

The answer to this is No, at the moment - but it has not been unknown. We
play for fun and S&B is not especially fun to play with or against (in our
Opinion). However there have been a few decks in the past, but most people
grow tired of what is a mindless strategy (when playing the game - not so
much when it comes to deck construction now)

2. The creativity argument, again (unfortunately): I said that CL does not
stiffle creativity very much - perhaps a little, but not to the extent that
many NL players seem to think. JH said that he has played under CL and found
that it was too restrictive.

To this I would counter that his group had not developed the style of play
under CL to the advanced stage that we have managed to attain.

2a. JH said that when you construct a deck under 4CL you WILL put in 4 of
every good card, and that means that deck creation requires less skill; he
said that when he played under 4CL they all did this.

ref to point 2 above

2b. JH said that a CL deck is forced into using more than one strategy as
the limit is too restrictive.

This is not always the case, but we find that any deck with out the ability
to to get rid of the last few points of blood (usually around 8 for against
a rush deck), by either bleeding or voting will be very slow at the final
ousting, and may well be ousted before he gets the chance to finish off his
victory (hence most combat decks - intercept of rush - would add a few
permanent bleed cards just to oust their prey.)

2c. I said that a deck would have to utilise more than the obvious to a
certain strategy to get that strategy to work. JH wanted to know why this
was better.

Well, this is just down to opinion, which is what I have been trying to
state all along - we like CL you like NL so lets just say fair's fair and go
home (please read my "Treaty of Sabbat" article).

3. The broken cards debate: I said that becase you have less of a broken
card in a deck it means that: i) that card will be less effective in the
long run (for action/combat cards, eg Thoughts Betrayed), or will not be
guaranteed of coming out - therefore a deck cannot rely on getting said card
into play, a deck cannot win if it relies on said card. JH said that this
was the same for NL.

The idea is that under CL the card will come up a lot less often therefore
you can't rely on it at all, rather than relying on it a little bit.

3a. broken cards sideline: Angelica. JH wanted to know how her master card
cycling ability is not broken under CL.

Because you won't have large amounts of master cards as most are unique and
you won't have more than one, therefore you will undoubtedly need all the
masters you have.

3b. I said that under a 1CL uniques environment Unnatural disaters are more
likely to be played as the card will be "permanently" countered as it will
never come out again, with there being only one of that card in the deck. JH
miss interperated this and thought that I was meaning that under CL you will
know how many cards someone has left in their deck of any given type. JH
also wanted to know why it was nessessary to permanently counter such a
location.

I suppose its not nessesary, but there is likewise no reason why its
unreasonable - we just do it for flavour and to increase the challenge -
which is what we like.

3c. Majesty debate: JH said that presence has three S:CE cards (I only have
seen two of these - majesty and Staredown; catatonic fear must be very rare
- does it let you untap as well?) and that Majesty casues big problems with
its repeat actions.

Hmm. So you have 12 S:CE's and probably only 8 anti S:CEs in your defense,
however - both the player's predator and prey will have 8 therefore its 12
Vs 16 is this a problem?

4. The Rush debate: Originally I said that the Sabbat was good because it
made rush under CL come back up to par with the NL version of the rush deck.
JH countered this by telling me that I have said that CL decks are better
than NL decks.

with respect to this point, I never said that CL decks were better than NL
decks (as an aside I did say that our group seems to have better decks than
most NL decks that I've seen on the Net) I was merely stating that, previous
to Sabbat, CL was not as good at rushing than NL, now there are extra cards
and CL rush becomes viable.

5. I said that Wizards of the Coast (WotC) must have been planning to fix
the problems in CL, as the cards that are slightly different duplicates in
the Sabbat expansion are geared towards fixing the problems with CL. JH said
that I couldn't say that WotC deliberately intended this.

Possibly not, but its one hell of a coincidence, especially considering that
its been happening since the arival of V:tES.

6. JH took the oportunity to slander myself and my friends and my fellow
students at Leeds Univerity.

This point is unfair and insulting - I have tried very hard not to be
insulting to JH, but he seems to find the urge insult me nonetheless - Ah
well. I believe that the problem with "Leeds" started sometime last sping,
when an aquaintance of our Jyhad group took it upon himself to have some fun
at our expense. We do not feel that any association with these events is
fair, please take back these comments.

7. I said that Card limits is a different way of fixing the game like GT, as
the game seems to be unplayable in its truely original form. I also said
that I personally prefer the CL environment game, JH decided that he'd
decide not to agree with me.

This is a problem that we CL players feel should be acknowledged - SOME NL
players seem to find the fact that we like CL insulting. We argue only that
one day all NL players will turn around and say "Well, its okay if you want
- I don't like it, but if you do, thats fine. Its not like its any worse or
anything". Please let us continue to play and stop telling us that NL is so
much better - we know what its like and don't like it so let us stick to
what we like. We want recognition as equals, not to be either gods or
ameoba's

8. Arguments on Fun: I said that I wanted CL to be recognised as a fun
environment to play in. JH said that he didn't agree with my opinion that CL
was more fun and that therefore I shouldn't play CL.

see above.

9. I said that a good CL deck rarely has to discard. JH does not seem to be
able to comprehend this fact - he said that the only advantage is that you
will not use up one of the four cards that you have in the deck.

This is the entire point that I was trying to make - under CL all your cards
are precious - therefore you are wasting if you are having to discard.

9a. I said that under CL you need to make sure that you don't waste cards
willy-nilly, that a deck that looses too many cards on wasted actions will
be doomed to inevitable failiure - JH took this to mean that if someone has
an S:CE then your entire rush is wasted.

This is not the case as you can have many rushes with a haven uncovered and
use all those S:CE's up. if you use up a Rush then one of eight rush for one
of 12 S:CEs (Then you think about 4 Havens) its not so scary. Hidden lurker
/ rush is pretty good too. you have to remember that you also have anti S:CE
cards as well as all that rush.

10. The Obf/Pre deck. this is probably the longest bit and although
effectively an aside will be dealt with here in total. Points:
a) I said that the deck was origionally posted as settites (include here the
quote; "Malks are no longer the problem - Now the settites become the broken
ones... the following deck...") After this he posted an alternative weenie
obf/pre bleed deck. and claimed that he didn't mention the settites, when in
actuality he did. He then claimed that I was saying his deck was bad because
it didn't use a single clan.

This was not my point I commented on what I was lead to believe was a
Settite only deck, which i'm sure everone would agree would not make a great

b) I said that it couldn't do especially scary bleeds. He said that it could
do 3 - 5 blood bleeds at up to +3 stealth.

Most of the vampires mentioned have inferior presence, and most who have

c) I said that it could quite happily be bleed bounced. JH claimed that

there are actually 16 bleed bounce cards available, and with actions you
have to declare them first, so you can counteract the majesty problems.

d) I said the deck can be intercepted. JH said that there was too much
stealth available for me to be able to do that.

Possibly, but theres as much intercept, especially considering Elder

e) I said that it would be very easily rushed and torporised. JH said that

deck would get the rush through quickly enough to pound the deck no problem.
JH said that deck size is not a viable tactic.

I think that You'll find deck size is an extremely good tactic.

f) JH said that his deck doesn't actually put in too many S:CE's, which was

so If you don't use majesties, how are you going to cause the big problems

11. the potence deck. Another deck has come into our discussions. follow as

and then contradicted himself by adding Taste of Vitae's (see below)

>>Any action granted by a card in play is a type distinct to that instance
>>of the card.

>If "Political Action" is an action type, what is the status of political
>actions granted by cards in play: are they allowed in multiples or not (say,
>can a single vampire attempt 2 actions to remove 2 distinct Archons ?)

Oops - not specific enough (again). Try this instead:
"Any non-rulebook action granted by a card in play..."

They are all of the "political action" type.

>I suppose actions granted to a minion by itself enter this class (like Etrius'

>> I find it distasteful to be able to rummage

>Could it not also be seen to be more "skillful" to be seen to have to

>uniques (even to a small degree)?

You argue for two entirely separate things - a 4CL generally and a 1CL on
uniques. These have no relation - you can have 4CL without any particular
restrictions on unique (the most common CL, actually) - and you can have
1CL on uniques in an otherwise NL environment (this has been advocated).
The 4CL business has been addressed elsewhere. My question is what
possible benefit do you get from a 1CL limit on uniques that you don't get
from simply saying that burned uniques cannot be brought back into the
game?

1CL is far less realistic for two reasons. First, if something is
destroyed, then another Methuseleh can brings it out. How can this other
Meth get something that no longer exists? Second, since you can only have
one copy in a deck, often you'll never see the card even come up. You
mean that if a Meth really wants control of the Rack, it can't get it?
Ridiculous.

1CL also creates a verification issue. With a "burned stays burned" rule,
you don't have to check anybody's deck to ensure compliance. Checking a
deck for a 1CL means you have to go through the whole deck before play.
Wouldn't you rather play?

Finally, there are some decks that simply don't work right if they don't
get certain specific uniques. More commonly, there are theme decks that
make less sense if they don't get certain uniques. I'm not aware of any
such decks that are abusive other than the ToR decks, so why would you
pointlessly reduce variety and flavor?

All the benefits you cite still operate. If somebody burns your hunting
grounds, it's gone, period.

So in summation, if you want uniques to be unique, a "burned stays burned"
rule provides the following advantages over a 1CL:

More realistic
Greater variety of non-abusive decks
Easier to enforce

In terms of CL vs. NL, the main effect of the new card substitutes is that
CL doesn't work like CL anymore. CL used to fundamentally alter the game
primarily by its effects on rush decks and carded combat decks. Rush
decks were impossible before DS and very restricted and stereotyped after.
Likewise carded combat was very difficult, although Brujah, Tremere, and
Gangrel could manage a passable job. The result was a game markedly
skewed to bleed and permanent votes, defended by gunnery. Now that there
are 3 disciplineless rush cards, and enough combat cards for a variety of
carded combat decks, the game will be much more like NL. The marked
characteristics of CL - intercept everywhere and permanents everywhere -
are going to be gone now. The central balance of Jyhad -
bleed/vote/combat vs. hosers for each - is now operational, whereas before
it wasn't.

Now many effects of card limits remain. The main one is simply that they
obliterate a huge variety of decks. Mono-clan decks, with access to three
disciplines, have a huge advantage over multi-clan decks, which usually
have access to only one discipline. Likewise a number of cards, such as
the Serpentis corruption cards or unduplicated combat cards such as
Apportation and Aid from Bats, make no sense unless present in quantity.
So you lose a heck of a lot of variety. You gain the limitation on
S:CE/untap decks of various ilks.

The puzzlement to me is that this option has always been available. 6CL,
or 10% CL, with the original set works basically like 4CL with all the
expansions. So why are the 4CL advocates generally happy with an
expansion that changes their game into a form they have rejected for 2
years?

If I were playing with Sabbat (I won't until and unless they print them
with Jyhad backs) I'd be willing to play 4CL today. Just like 6CL before,
it's Jyhad - limited significantly, but meaningfully Jyhad. I'd still
prefer NL, of course.

Curt Adams (curt...@aol.com)

Well, I might disagree here. I realize that some people are uncomfortable
with allowing a minion to "attack" more than once in a turn since it gives
combat decks an advantage that political and bleed decks don't have.
However, it seems to me that this is balanced against the bleed decks'
advantage of their primary action being cardless, i.e. they don't have to
wait for their library to produce a card so that they can perform their
design function.
Against the political deck this is not the case since it also has to have
a card in hand to perform it's primary function. But a political deck
will have a higher proportion of political action cards in it than a
combat deck will have get-into-combat cards. And political cards are
useful for something other than calling the action: they can be tossed for
votes. It seems to me that political action cards can be put into a deck
at a reliably high proportion and not hurt the political deck's primary
purpose, passing votes, but the get-into-combat cards have to be carefully
mixed into a combat deck to allow reliability without hurting the combat
effectiveness. This seems to be a built-in disadvantage of rush decks. I
don't think there is such a problem with minions attacking multiple times
in a turn that a change or house rule is needed. But of course if a group
feels differently about it then a house rule would be easy enough to
devise I think.
Just my opinion.

There is one rule: A minion may not attempt the same type of action more
than once each turn.

A "type" is:
Any action type described in the rulebook.
For actions not described therein, each action card is its own type (type
defined by card name) while each action bestowed by a card in play is its own
type (type defined by individual card in play).

(These "sub-rules", as you call them, were generated for Change of Target,
so 4CL has exactly the same sub-rules defining what "same action" means).
